brief: Goldman's Privorotsky: hedge funds are aggressively unwinding AI longs and systematic strategies are taking losses, with Goldman's Equity Systematic L/S estimate down 2.17% last week (worst since December 2023), Fundamental L/S net exposure back to the 7th percentile on index short covering, single stocks sold for seven straight weeks, and retail sentiment deeply bearish. The reset is real but not confirmed finished. Goldman's Risk Appetite Indicator posted one of its largest October declines yet sits above the -1 contrarian-buy level; after the 11 largest RAI declines since 2005 the S&P 500 returned -17% to +7% over one month and -32% to +18% over six months, so the reset does not guarantee a bottom either way. Separately, Garrett notes single-stock and credit volatility have priced stress for weeks while index volatility only now catches up: SPX 12-month implied correlation sits near 20%, among the lowest on record, even as the crowd, caught short vol into the panic, chases expensive protection, and 2026's upside-vol regime flips toward downside vol and pricier insurance. JPMorgan counters that the S&P 500 has risen 6, 9 and 12 months after every midterm election since 1990 (averaging 11.4%, 12.5%, 14.7%), and with momentum exposure at 30% of peak and broad hedge fund deleveraging, conditions favor an alpha rebound even though the de-risking is not yet capitulatory.
